title: Canonical coordinate sections and their eventual polynomial
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $N\ge0$, $B=k[z_0,\ldots,z_N]$ with total-degree grading, and $J\subseteq B$ a homogeneous ideal. Give the actual quotient $A=B/J=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}A_m$ its quotient grading [def-sfb-coordinate-quotient-grading], and write $u_j$ for the image of $z_j$. Let $i:Z=\operatorname{Proj}(A)\hookrightarrow P=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ be the quotient closed immersion [def-pc-proj, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $L_m=i^*\widetilde{B(m)}$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. For every $m\ge0$ there is a canonical isomorphism $\theta_m:\widetilde{A(m)}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_m$. On $D_+(u_j)$ it sends $u_j^m$ to the pulled-back basis $e_j$ corresponding to $z_j^m$; the transition is $e_i=(u_i/u_j)^m e_j$. Define $\sigma_m:A_m\to H^0(Z,L_m)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] by the compatible restrictions $h\mapsto(h/u_j^m)e_j$. This map is $k$-linear. Every $A_m$ is finite-dimensional, and there are $a\ge0$ and $P_J\in\mathbf Q[t]$ such that for every $m\ge a$, $\sigma_m$ is an isomorphism and $P_J(m)=\dim_k A_m=\dim_k H^0(Z,L_m)$. No saturation or nonemptiness is assumed. The statement includes $J=B$, with zero quotient, and empty standard charts.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, for the actual quotient graded ring; constructions.tex Tag 01MT, lemma-apply-modules, and Tag 01N1, lemma-surjective-graded-rings-generated-degree-1-map-proj, for the chartwise pullback comparison; algebra.tex Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, for the eventual polynomial.

proof.text: If $J=B$, then $A=0$ and $Z=\varnothing$ by [def-pc-proj]; all modules, sheaves and sections in the conclusion are zero, so take $a=0$ and $P_J=0$. Henceforth $J\ne B$. A nonzero constant in $J$ would be a unit, so $J\cap k=0$ and $A_0=k$. By [def-sfb-coordinate-quotient-grading], the quotient map is degree-preserving and the $u_j$ generate $A$ in degree one. Thus $A$ is standard graded [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], and is a finite graded module over itself, generated by $1$. The field $A_0=k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. The $D_+(u_j)$ cover $Z$: a homogeneous prime containing all $u_j$ contains $A_+$ and is not a Proj point.

source.place: Tag 00JL, section-graded: homogeneous quotient; standard degree-one generation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison] to $B\twoheadrightarrow A$, and invert its twist isomorphism to obtain $\theta_m:\widetilde{A(m)}\simeq i^*\widetilde{B(m)}=L_m$. Its chart formula sends $u_j^m$ to $e_j$. In the localized degree-$m$ module of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], $u_i^m=(u_i/u_j)^m u_j^m$ on an overlap. Applying $\theta_m$ gives $e_i=(u_i/u_j)^m e_j$, including when a chart is empty.

Use the canonical $A_0$-linear section map $c_m:A_m\to H^0(Z,\widetilde{A(m)})$ of [lem-sfb-finite-graded-module-section-tail]. Its restriction is $h/1=(h/u_j^m)u_j^m$ by the shifted-localization formula [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. Hence $H^0(\theta_m)c_m$ has precisely the compatible restrictions defining $\sigma_m$. This proves existence and $k$-linearity of $\sigma_m$ in every degree, not only in the tail. The hypotheses of the cited tail theorem hold by step 1 (extend the grading of $A$ by zero in negative degrees). It gives $a_1\ge0$ with $c_m$, and therefore $\sigma_m$, an isomorphism for every $m\ge a_1$.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module; constructions.tex Tag 01MT, lemma-apply-modules, canonical section map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-standard-graded-hilbert-function] with $S=M=A$, using the standard grading and cyclic module generation checked in step 1. It gives finite-dimensionality of every $A_m$, a polynomial $P_J\in\mathbf Q[t]$ and $a_2\ge0$ with $P_J(m)=\dim_k A_m$ for $m\ge a_2$. Take $a=\max(a_1,a_2)$. For $m\ge a$, the $k$-linear isomorphism $\sigma_m$ carries a basis of $A_m$ to a basis of $H^0(Z,L_m)$, giving the second dimension equality. No step required saturation, or a nonempty chart or scheme.
